To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have implemented an FPGA GZIP compression core and tested it against a software GZIP implementation.
we have implemented a GZIP compressor for FPGA that is at least 2× faster than software compression on an i7 processor, for all scenarios, and up 18× faster on large files.
we have designed, implemented, and tested a complete, open source GZIP compression system for FPGA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the design and implementation of a systolic array based GZIP hardware compressor for FPGA, (2) the development and evaluation of a software application to control the FPGA hardware compressor, and (3) an evaluation of our FPGA compressor against a software implementation of the same algorithm.
the design, implementation and evaluation of a hardware-based GZIP compressor for FPGAs.
the design of hardware accelerators to offload computationally expensive compression tasks from the CPU, thereby improving the performance of compression-based distributed systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present an open-source GZIP implementation for FPGA which is at least twice faster than the best software implementation.
the FPGA GZIP implementation presented here is an efficient, high performance, open-source solution for compressing files in real-time.
we have designed, implemented, and evaluated an FPGA GZIP compression system which can be used to compress files at high speed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we designed, implemented and evaluated a hardware GZIP compression core for FPGA.
we present the first complete, open-source, FPGA GZIP compression system, with a systolic compression core, and a software application to interface with the FPGA.
we have developed and implemented a complete, open source GZIP compressor in FPGA, and we have demonstrated that it outperforms software compression by a large margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the FPGA GZIP compression solution presented in this paper can be used to accelerate distributed systems such as HPC clusters, where compression and decompression of data are the bottleneck of the system performance.
FPGA-based compression is a viable alternative to software-based compression for large-scale data processing applications.
hardware compression can be used to improve the performance of compression in distributed systems, and that hardware compression can also be used to accelerate software-based compression.
